name: One Happy Workation (Remote Worker Stay)

requirements.blocker_text: Must be employed by, or self-employed through, a company or business based in the applicant's home country -- income must not come from an Aruban company.
Must book a participating hotel/resort package and select 'One Happy Workation' as the visit purpose on the ED card -- there is no separate government application.
Minimum stay 1 week; maximum stay 90 days total, including any extension.

evidence_required.document: Completed ED card selecting 'One Happy Workation' as visit purpose
Proof of foreign employment or self-employment

sources.title: Aruba Tourism Authority -- One Happy Workation: eligibility (foreign employment/self-employment only, no Aruban-sourced income), 1 week to 90 day duration, package-booking-only application process, explicit non-residency confirmation

notes: STATUS: DRAFT (tier-3 sourcing throughout -- ATA is not the immigration authority). NEW ROUTE, part of Aruba's initial build. This is NOT a separate visa or DIMAS-issued permit -- it is a marketing/administrative program run by the Aruba Tourism Authority (ATA), a statutory tourism-promotion body, layered on top of the standard visitor entry (see aw_visitor_visa.json): the applicant remains a visitor for immigration-status purposes, simply declaring remote-work intent on the ED card and booking a participating package. Tier 3 rather than tier 1 since ATA is not the immigration authority (DIMAS); modelled as its own route rather than folded into aw_visitor_visa.json because it has a materially different, explicitly documented eligibility test (foreign-sourced income only, no work for an Aruban company) and a distinct declared purpose-of-visit. work_rights is 'restricted' to reflect that only foreign-sourced remote work is permitted, not local employment. The source explicitly confirms this route does NOT lead to Aruba resident registration or any immigration status beyond the visitor stay.
